clue.text: Cup — runner holds it during service

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it inside, so MASS takes IT in
what happens during an event sits inside it, so the service sits inside the runner

blocks.note: the Dee is a river, and a river is a runner

explanation.surface: A cup is passed round during a church service while someone holds it.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest, one inside the other. 'Runner' for a river is a standard crossword convention, since rivers run.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a demitasse is one kind of cup, the small one used for strong coffee.

clue.text: King spoiling absurd plan

indicators.note: a spoiler breaks into something, so the king breaks into DAFT

explanation.surface: A king ruins a ridiculous scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: R for king comes from the Latin rex, as in the royal signature ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a draft is a first, rough plan of something to be written or built.

clue.text: Sailor finds companion on piece of land

blocks.note: a lot is a plot of land

explanation.surface: A sailor comes ashore and finds a friend on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'on' simply puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional use: matelot, French for sailor, is British slang for a seaman.

clue.text: See 23
Gun crime at a higher level getting criticism initially

indicators.note: 'initially' here means first in order, so the criticism comes before the higher level

blocks.note: to get stick is to be criticised

explanation.surface: Armed crime rising sharply draws criticism from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' wants to take a first letter, but here it only sets the order of the two pieces. 'Stick' as criticism is British informal usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a stick-up, an armed hold-up, is one gun crime.

clue.text: English books inclined to be involved

blocks.note: NT = New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: English literature is inclined to get tangled up in itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Books' as the New Testament is a common crossword convention, alongside OT for the Old.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words mean caught up in something complicated.

clue.text: Hit — almost hit back

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so its last letter goes
going back means running the other way, so the letters are read from the end

blocks.note: KNOCK, a hit, 'almost': last letter dropped

explanation.surface: A boxer's blow is nearly returned in kind.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word does two jobs: the first 'Hit' is the definition, the second is the word to trim and turn round.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal synonym: to conk someone is to hit them, usually on the head.

clue.text: Red skirts — rip off skirting

indicators.note: to skirt is to run round the edge, so the rip-off goes round the other piece

blocks.note: rims skirt things, running round their edges

explanation.surface: An outraged complaint that red skirts are a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skirts' looks like the garment, but it is the verb for running round an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: crimson is one shade of red, deep and slightly purple.

clue.text: Compound of zinc's the cure in the end for German intellect

indicators.note: a compound is a mixture, so these letters are mixed together
'in the end' takes only the final letter of cure

explanation.surface: A zinc compound, ultimately, is the cure for a German mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound' reads as chemistry, zinc and all, but it asks for the letters to be mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Friedrich Nietzsche, the philosopher, is one German intellect.

clue.text: Voices raised in terrible argument, referee initially knocked over by players

indicators.note: 'initially' takes the first letter of each of the four words before it
something knocked over lies the other way round, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: a cast is the set of players in a show
first letters of in, terrible, argument, referee

explanation.surface: Players shout at each other in a fierce row and knock the referee down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' reaches back over all four words, not just 'referee'. 'By players' puts the cast beside the reversed letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Castrati were male singers castrated before puberty, so their voices were raised in pitch for life; the phrase also hints at the operation.

clue.text: Capital idea to start with, after one's broken record

indicators.note: a record broken open lets another letter in
'to start with' takes the first letter of idea
'after' puts the idea's letter behind the broken record

explanation.surface: Someone has a great idea just after smashing a record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like an old-fashioned exclamation praising the idea, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Taipei is one capital city, that of Taiwan.

clue.text: In opposite directions, lacquered metalware taken

indicators.note: two opposite compass points, south and north, go one on each side

blocks.note: tole is lacquered or painted tin ware

explanation.surface: Lacquered trays are carried off in two directions at once.
explanation.walkthrough: Tole is a decorative-craft word worth knowing: painted tin trays and boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: stolen goods have been taken without permission.

clue.text: Big college that is accommodating unknown number

indicators.note: to accommodate is to house, so 'that is' takes the unknown inside

explanation.surface: A large college houses an uncounted number of students.
explanation.walkthrough: King's is a well-known Cambridge college. Z is an algebra unknown, alongside X and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: king-size means extra large, as in a bed or a cigarette.

clue.text: See 19
Variety in a wine list a growing concern for heavy drinkers, perhaps?

definitions.text: a growing concern for heavy drinkers, perhaps?

indicators.note: variety means a different arrangement, so these letters come in a new order

explanation.surface: A varied wine list tempts heavy drinkers, a worrying prospect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growing concern' is a business phrase for a thriving firm, but here it is something that literally grows.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition: a heavy drinker's waistline expands, so it is both growing and a concern.

clue.text: Evidence hack, say, was there to find clue — nothing concerning promotion in it

indicators.note: 'in it' puts the preceding letters inside the clue word just given

explanation.surface: Hunting for proof that a journalist was on the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' reads as a journalist, but it is an ordinary riding horse, and 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a hoofprint is the mark proving a horse, such as a hack, passed that way.

clue.text: Jumper in equestrian sport with narrow margin of victory

blocks.note: winning by a neck in a horse race

explanation.surface: A show jumper wins an equestrian event by a whisker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' reads as a horse, which fits the surface; it is the British word for a sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a polo neck, a turtleneck in American English, is one kind of jumper.

clue.text: Glassy expression's first seen in very upset suitor

indicators.note: 'first' takes the opening letter of expression
an upset suitor is thrown into disorder, so his letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rejected suitor wears a glassy, blank expression.
explanation.walkthrough: The E joins the suitor's letters before they are mixed, and V stands in front of the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: vitreous, from Latin vitrum, glass, means glassy.

clue.text: See 22
Greek song others performed around piano

indicators.note: a piece performed is worked into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged
the rearranged letters go around the piano

explanation.surface: Other people sang a Greek song round the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piano' belongs to the singing picture, but it is only the musical marking for soft.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a strophe is one part of an ancient Greek choral ode, sung by the chorus.

clue.text: Electrical device — more foolish instrument of punishment

blocks.note: dim = foolish, so dimmer = more foolish
a switch is a thin cane for beating

explanation.surface: A gadget that is sillier than the rest, like a tool for punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs on from 19 across into 12 across. A switch is a flexible stick once used for beating.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a dimmer switch, which varies a light's brightness, is one electrical device.

clue.text: With drunken glee I'm glugging absinthe to begin with — how far gone?

indicators.note: 'to begin with' takes the first letter of absinthe
to glug a drink is to take it in, so the fodder swallows the A
drunken letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A merry drinker downs absinthe and wonders how drunk they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How far gone?' reads as how drunk, but it asks about distance travelled.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is a question the answer settles: a car's mileage records the distance it has covered.

clue.text: Southern frontiersman, big chap

blocks.note: trappers worked the frontier for furs

explanation.surface: A burly man from the Southern frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma hides a join: 'big chap' is the definition, not a description of the frontiersman.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal synonym: a strapper is a big, strongly built person, as in 'strapping lad'.

clue.text: Feed unlimited dill, in herbaceous plant

indicators.note: without limits means without its ends, so only the middle of dill is kept
'in' puts the trimmed dill inside the plant

explanation.surface: Advice to feed a herb plant plenty of dill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feed' reads as an instruction, but it is the noun, and it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: silage, fermented grass stored for winter, is one kind of animal feed.

clue.text: Scanning text quickly, Twitter covering fear of urinals?

indicators.note: to cover something is to wrap round it, so the twitter goes round the fear

blocks.note: to twitter is to sing, as birds do

explanation.surface: Reading posts fast on Twitter about a phobia of public toilets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twitter' looks like the social network, but it is birdsong. The answer runs on from 22 down into 17 down.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: speed reading is the trained skill of skimming a page at pace.

clue.text: Ride straight on up the creek

indicators.note: up the creek means in trouble, so the letters are in disarray

explanation.surface: A boat trip heading straight on up a creek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up the creek' is an idiom for being in trouble. The answer runs on from 23 down into 3 down.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a ghost train, a fairground ride through a spooky dark tunnel, is one ride.

clue.text: Car from Providence somewhere in Italy

blocks.note: Providence is the capital of Rhode Island, abbreviated RI
the Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: A car shipped from Providence ends up in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Providence' looks like fate, but it is the city standing for its state. 'From' puts the car after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Rimini, a resort on the Adriatic coast, is one place in Italy.

clue.text: Hunter, head in plaster bloodied on a rock

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: A taken as printed; 'on' just joins
a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: A hunter's head is bandaged and bloody after a fall on a rock.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a craggy outcrop on a hilltop, as on Dartmoor in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a predator is an animal that hunts others.

clue.text: Sponge cakes right for composer

indicators.note: to cake is to coat thickly, so the begging word coats the R

blocks.note: to sponge is to cadge or beg

explanation.surface: A composer is rewarded with sponge cakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sponge cakes' reads as a noun phrase, but 'sponge' is a verb for begging and 'cakes' means coats.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Alban Berg, the Austrian who wrote the opera Wozzeck, is one composer.

clue.text: Most happening to see border in Italian city that's not closed

indicators.note: 'not closed' leaves the city's name open at the end, dropping its final E
'in' puts the border inside the shortened city

blocks.note: TRIESTE with its last letter removed
an end is a border or edge

explanation.surface: Crossing an open border into Italy's liveliest city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not closed' is a neat way to say the last letter is missing: the word is left open at its end.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Happening' is informal for fashionable, so the most happening is the trendiest.
